source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: Can I interpret a digital root as remainder information rather than just a digit-sum procedure?

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Repeated digit sum is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Can I interpret a digital root as remainder information rather than' is answered as repeated digit sum rather than digital root.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Repeated digit sum is what produces digital root, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Can I interpret a digital root as remainder information.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The answer is digital root because of the most obvious label, colour, size or printed number in the stem, without using 'Can I interpret a digital root as remainder information rather than' as the operative test.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: digital root is settled by running 'Can I decide when the sum of two even numbers is a multiple of 4?': Every even number is either a multiple of 4 or 2 more than a multiple of 4. The sum of two — on the item about Can I interpret a digital root as remainder information.

intelligence.enrichment: The digital root of a number is the single digit obtained by repeatedly adding its digits. In the divisibility-by-9 setting, repeated digit sums keep the same remainder information, and multiples of 9 have digital root 9.
